summary: Alert Tagging: operators attach/remove free-form tags on alerts, filter GET /api/alerts by tag, tags returned in AlertResponse.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new Tag entity exists with a many-to-many relationship to Alert, persisted via a new join table and a new EF migration (database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql regenerated).
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags accepts one or more tags and adds them to the alert; returns 404 if the alert does not exist.
POST dedupes tags case-insensitively (within the request and against tags already on the alert); a duplicate does not create a second assignment.
POST rejects with 400 any tag whose length is not 1-30 characters (after trimming) and any request that would leave the alert with more than 10 tags; nothing is persisted on rejection.
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes the tag assignment and returns 204; returns 404 if the alert does not exist or the tag is not assigned to that alert.
GET /api/alerts accepts an optional 'tag' query parameter and returns only alerts carrying that tag.
The 'tag' filter composes (AND) with existing filters isActive, severity, createdFrom/createdTo and search, and with paging/sorting/TotalCount.
AlertResponse includes the alert's tags on every endpoint that returns it (list, get by id, create, update, deactivate, add-tags).

scope_anchors: Alert entity + new Tag entity + EF configuration/migration
constraints: Scope exceeds the 5-source-file cap deliberately: the story crosses Models, Data.SQL (config, migration), Data, Common, DTO, Service, Controller layers.
Keep layering Controller -> IAlertService -> IAlertRepository -> AlertDbContext; controller stays HTTP-only, entities never leave the service layer.
Tag filter and tag add/remove must be parameterized EF queries (no raw SQL / string concatenation); tag path/query values are untrusted input and must be length-validated.
Tag assignments must be removed when an alert is deleted (cascade on the join table).
Migration is generated with dotnet-ef (dotnet-tools.json), never hand-edited snapshot; update database/02_AlertServiceDb_Migrations.sql per database standard.
GET list and GET by id must load tags (Include) to avoid N+1; tag filter must not duplicate alert rows.
coverage_goals: Every acceptance criterion AC1-AC8 covered by at least one passing test; tag add/remove/filter branches covered at behavior level.
missing_facts: HTTP status/body for POST tags on success (assumed 200 with updated AlertResponse) - see plan.md assumptions
HTTP status when 10-tag limit is exceeded (assumed 400 ProblemDetails/ValidationProblemDetails)
Tag character set restrictions beyond length 1-30 (assumed none; free-form, trimmed)
unresolved_questions: Should tag casing of first-added form be preserved for display (assumed yes) while matching/filtering/deleting is case-insensitive?
Should orphaned Tag rows (no remaining assignments) be deleted when the last assignment is removed (assumed no; cleanup deferred)?
Should POST fail entirely or silently skip when every submitted tag already exists on the alert (assumed idempotent 200, no error)?
